blocks.text: When there are two functional groups available for the formation of a bond or bridging linkage to create the polymeric chains, the condensation polymerisation takes place. Mostly, a small molecule is removed from the two monomers during the formation of the polymer. The two functional group may exist in a single molecule (e.g. lactic acid) or two different molecules, as in the case of nylon 6,6.
The common functional groups that can undergo condensation polymerisation are:

items: amino group (NH₂) and carboxylic (COOH) group (polyamide and H₂O)
amin group (NH₂) and acyl chlorides (COCl) (polyamide and HCl)
carboxylic group (COOH) and alcohols (OH) (polyester and H₂O)
acyl chlorides (COCl) and alcohols (OH) (polyester and HCl).

blocks.text: Give the structures of the polymers formed from the monomers. For each polymer identify the following:

items: the attractive force between the polymer chains.

blocks.explanation: The –OH of one molecule joins the –COOH of another with loss of H₂O, so a polyester forms. Repeat unit: [–O–C₆H₄–CO–]ₙ; linkage: ester; forces between the chains: permanent dipole–dipole forces between the polar ester groups and van der Waals (London) forces between the rings.

blocks.alt: A benzene ring with a C(=O)OH group (O drawn up, HO down) and OH at the opposite (para) position.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 26.2 a) the monomer (original drawing after the structure printed in the textbook on PDF page 154).

blocks.explanation: The –NH₂ and –COOH groups join with loss of H₂O, so a polyamide forms. Repeat unit: [–NH–C₆H₄–NH–CO–C₅H₈–CO–]ₙ; linkage: amide; forces between the chains: hydrogen bonds between the N–H of one chain and the C=O of another, together with van der Waals forces.

blocks.alt: H2N-C6H4-NH2 (a benzene ring with NH2 at opposite positions) + a cyclopentane ring carrying two C(=O)OH groups on alternate carbons.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 26.2 b) the monomers (original drawing after the structure printed in the textbook on PDF page 154).
